human_facing_meta_review.author_guidance: To strengthen evidential support and reproducibility, please: (1) retrain embeddings only on training partitions (per CV fold and in temporal holdouts) and report how this changes LexExt composition and all main results; (2) provide an annotated sample for Risk Factors extraction with extraction metrics and examples of errors; (3) perform company-grouped CV and temporal holdouts and report metrics; (4) publish per-fold predictions and compute paired statistical tests (or bootstrap CIs) for the primary comparisons; (5) add sensitivity/ablation studies for similarity threshold (e.g., 0.6–0.9), top-k expansion (5/10/20), PCA dims (50/200/400/800), and SVM hyperparameters including RBF gamma, and run out-of-fold stacking and alternate meta-learners; (6) report details and tuning for mklaren/MKL or include a better-tuned MKL baseline; (7) report how many labels were removed by mean ±3σ filtering and provide results without filtering (or with robust losses) and tail-focused metrics; and (8) release code, seeds, exact fold splits, and preprocessing scripts (or a container) to allow independent replication. In re-submission, include a concise table comparing original vs corrected pipelines to show the impact of each remedial change.
human_facing_meta_review.comments:
Summary:
The paper adapts embedding-augmented IR term-weighting to lexicon-based sentiment on 10-K Risk Factors and reports improved volatility prediction (B̂M25) and stronger Text+Market performance via stacking on a 2012–2015 subset. The study includes temporal clustering diagnostics and sector analyses.

Strengths:
- Clear pipeline mapping IR embedding-augmentation (Eq.3) to lexicon-weight features and end-to-end regression. 
- Broad empirical comparisons (weighting variants, lexicon expansions, fusion strategies, baselines) and interpretable sector analyses.
- Practical fusion recommendation: stacking shows strong empirical performance in the reported experiments.

Limitations:
- Word2Vec trained on entire corpus risks temporal leakage; no retraining-per-fold experiments reported. This is a major threat to the validity of embedding-augmented gains.
- Risk Factors (Item 1A) extraction is heuristic and unvalidated (no annotated precision/recall); extraction errors could bias text features.
- Cross-validation details do not clarify company-grouping; multiple reports per company raise company-level leakage concerns.
- Hyperparameter and pipeline choices (threshold=0.70, top-20 expansion, PCA=400, fixed SVM settings, stacking 70/30) are under-documented and not ablated; rankings may be sensitive.
- No fold-level variances or statistical tests are reported, hindering assessment of significance and robustness.
- Outlier filtering (mean ±3σ) removes extreme volatility labels without reporting counts or sensitivity; this may bias practical risk-relevant performance.

Open Questions:
- Were Word2Vec and LexExt trained on the full corpus including test-year documents? Please provide experiments with embeddings trained only on training partitions and report effects on main results.
- Provide an annotated Risk Factors extraction validation set (and extraction metrics). How robust are results to using validated extractions?
- Are CV folds grouped by company? If not, rerun grouped CV and temporal holdouts and report differences in r2/MSE and variance.
- Supply per-fold metrics and perform paired statistical tests (or bootstrap CIs) for primary comparisons (B̂M25 vs baselines; stacking vs MKL/early fusion). Are differences significant?
- Provide ablation/sensitivity studies for similarity threshold, top-k expansion size, PCA dimension, SVM gamma/C/epsilon, and stacking protocol (out-of-fold stacking). How stable are method rankings?
- How many volatility labels did the mean ±3σ filter remove, and how do results change when that filtering is removed or when robust loss/tail metrics are used?

Transparency:
Missing critical reproducibility details: Word2Vec hyperparameters and whether embeddings were trained per-fold, Risk Factors extraction rules and lack of annotated validation, exact CV partitioning policy (company-grouped or report-level), hyperparameter search logs for PCA and SVM (including RBF gamma), mklaren/MKL parameterization, counts of labels removed by filtering, and per-fold metric outputs. Release of code, seeds, exact folds, embedding training scripts, and the annotated extraction validation set is necessary for independent replication.

confidence_interval.rationale: Moderate uncertainty: reviewers consistently found plausible and coherent evidence that embedding-augmented weighting and stacking can improve volatility prediction under the reported pipeline, but their shared, repeated identification of major methodological risks (temporal/company-level leakage, unvalidated extraction, missing sensitivity analyses, and absent statistical tests) implies a meaningful chance that some or much of the numerical improvement will shrink or lose significance after remediation. The interval reflects that outcome is plausible but not certain; resolving the listed reproducibility checks would materially increase confidence.
